name: invoke_library_vector_minus_258
description: Clamps the two coordinate arguments so neither is negative and each stays inside limits read from a structure that the first argument points to, then forwards them to a library function at offset minus 258 from a library base.

name: format_string_with_directives
description: Copies a format string into an output buffer, turning each doubled percent sign into one percent sign and expanding other percent directives through a called routine that fills a temporary buffer. It writes a terminating zero at the end.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and then returns. It takes no arguments of its own and adds no processing around the call.

name: dispatch_one_or_five_calls
description: When both values in the first operand pair are zero, it calls a routine once with the argument three. Otherwise it calls a routine five times in a row when the second pair or the masked low value is non-zero, and returns unchanged if neither test passes.

name: check_and_repeat_call
description: Calls another routine five times in a row when a flag in one register or the masked value in another register is non-zero. Otherwise it returns without further action.

name: divide_double_words_bitwise
description: Performs a 32-step restoring division on pairs of 32-bit words. Each step shifts the working words left, subtracts the divisor pair from the running remainder when it fits, and records the bit that comes out.

name: run_three_calls_when_nonzero
description: When both operand pairs contain a non-zero value, it calls a routine twice, runs a countdown loop whose overflow branch the self-comparison test never takes, and then calls the routine a third time. Otherwise it returns.

name: run_three_calls_when_nonzero
description: When both operand pairs contain a non-zero value, it calls a routine twice, runs a countdown loop whose overflow branch the self-comparison test never takes, and then calls the routine a third time. Otherwise it returns.

name: run_three_calls_unconditionally
description: Calls a routine twice, runs a countdown branch that the self-comparison test never enables, then calls the routine once more and returns.

name: delay_then_call_routine
description: Runs a 16-bit countdown loop that starts from the low word of the third data register, then calls another routine and returns.

name: delay_if_small_then_call
description: If the zero flag is clear and the low word of the third data register is below 64, it runs a countdown loop starting from that value. It then calls another routine and returns.

name: delay_then_call_routine
description: Runs a 16-bit countdown loop that starts from the low word of the third data register, then calls another routine and returns.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one other routine and then returns. It takes no arguments of its own and adds no processing around the call.

name: scale_called_result_saturating
description: Calls a routine for a value, then shifts that value right by an amount taken from the low word of the input. It saturates to the largest positive value when the shift count is not negative, and returns zero when the input is zero.

name: scale_signed_result_by_count
description: Calls a routine for a value and shifts it right by an amount derived from the second input, saturating to the largest positive value when that amount is not negative. A negative second input negates the result, and a negative low word returns zero.

name: shift_and_sign_extend
description: Right-shifts the first input by the negated low word of the second input, and negates the result when the second input is negative. It returns the result in the data register.

name: invoke_library_vector_minus_84
description: Loads a library base from a global variable and calls the library routine at offset minus 84 from it, then returns. It passes no arguments of its own.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a zero-terminated string for the given character and returns a pointer to its first match, or null if it is absent. The terminating zero is also tested as a match candidate.

name: forward_two_arguments_unused
description: Forwards its two arguments to another routine and then returns. Nothing reaches this entry and the code sits in a gap that may be data, so it is an unused forwarder.

name: divide_unsigned_restoring
description: Returns zero when either input is zero. Otherwise it runs 32 shift-and-subtract steps, leaving the quotient of the first input divided by the second in the first value.

name: run_selection_loop_over_table
description: Makes a fixed sequence of library calls and pointer-based setup, then loops reading a selection value. When the value lies between two and eight, it walks seven table entries and forwards their fields to another routine, and the loop ends once the value reads as one, followed by a cleanup call.

name: iterate_table_entries_until_done
description: Repeatedly reads a value and, when it lies between two and eight, walks seven table entries and forwards selected fields to another routine. It stops when the stored value becomes one, then makes closing calls through a library vector.

name: forward_three_offset_calls
description: Calls another routine three times with fixed leading arguments, passing the input plus zero, four and eight as the last argument each time.

name: position_entry_and_forward_calls
description: Makes one call with constant arguments, then calls another routine with position values built from the two inputs plus fixed offsets, and finishes with a call whose value is read from a table indexed by the third input.

name: run_case_specific_call_sequence
description: For a parameter from two to eight it runs a fixed sequence of calls with constant coordinates and arguments, with another call between each step. A parameter of one or less does nothing extra.

name: return_without_action
description: Does nothing and returns. The body is a bare return with no calls or data access.

name: forward_two_values_to_call
description: Forwards its two word-sized arguments, together with a fixed base value, to another routine and then returns. No known caller reaches this entry.

name: run_table_driven_update_loop
description: Runs a counted loop that walks a 19-entry table on each pass and forwards each entry's values to another routine. When the mode argument is one it also walks a zero-terminated list of pairs, then sets flags for a closing step and makes several cleanup calls.

name: resume_table_update_loop
description: A stack-frame variant of the table update loop that resumes at its outer loop, walking the 19-entry table and the pair list with state kept in local frame slots. It exits through the same cleanup calls once the pass counter reaches zero.

name: continue_table_update_pass
description: Continues a table update pass from the point after the first step, decrementing a counter and walking the 19-entry table on each iteration. When the counter reaches zero it makes the closing calls and returns.

name: advance_table_update_step
description: Advances the table update step by incrementing a frame counter, then runs the 19-entry table pass and the pair list when it is the first step. It leaves through the closing calls once the counter reaches zero.

name: finish_table_update_cleanup
description: Makes two calls with a shared global argument, repeats one of them when a frame value is non-zero, then calls another routine and returns. It is the cleanup tail of the table update loop.

name: call_with_fixed_parameter_block
description: Calls another routine once with a fixed list of constant numeric parameters, taking two of them from a structure pointed to by a global value.

name: poll_until_ready_then_call
description: Calls one routine with a constant, then calls another with a global argument, polls a routine repeatedly until it returns one, and makes a final call with the same global argument.

name: unpack_float_mantissa_pair
description: Strips the sign bit from the first input and, when the input is non-zero, shifts the second input's bits into the mantissa position ten steps long and sets the top bit to form a normalised pair. A zero input gives zero for both words.

name: shift_sign_bits_into_word
description: Shifts the second input left ten times, collecting each outgoing sign bit into the first input, then sets the top bit of the result and returns it.

name: normalize_mantissa_check_range
description: Normalises a 64-bit mantissa pair by shifting it until its leading bit is in place and adjusting an exponent word to match. When the exponent falls below its valid range it calls a report routine with one, and above the range it calls it with two.

name: pack_normalized_double
description: Normalises a 64-bit mantissa by shifting until a leading bit is set, then packs the exponent and mantissa into a double-precision pair. An exponent below range calls a report routine with one and returns zero, and one above range calls it with two and returns an infinity pattern.

name: signal_one_return_zero
description: Calls a routine with the argument one and returns a zero double-precision value.

name: signal_two_return_infinity
description: Calls a routine with the argument two and returns a double-precision value with the maximum exponent and no mantissa, which is an infinity.

name: store_param_to_global
description: Copies its single argument into a global variable and returns. It performs no other operation.

name: copy_block_then_call_pointer
description: When its buffer argument is non-null, copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed offset in the data area into that buffer. It then calls through a function pointer held in a register and returns.

name: fill_handler_block_from_list
description: Scans a linked list for the largest entry value, then makes calls through a function pointer and fills a new block with a counting pattern of words. It copies a parameter block into place, stores the address of its own routine in the block, and returns zero on success or minus one when a call reports failure.

name: parse_startup_argument_string
description: Stores the startup argument string and splits it into words at spaces, honouring quoted strings and turning the star-N and star-E escapes into a newline and an escape character. It builds a pointer table for the words, then calls operating system routines for the current task and the reply, and returns zero.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers held at fixed negative offsets from a base register, then returns. No known caller reaches this entry, so it may be unused.

name: open_dos_library_with_setup
description: Opens the DOS library by name through the system library vector and returns the result if the open succeeded. On failure it runs a setup call, stores the value one hundred, runs cleanup calls when a flag is set, and returns that stored value.

name: forward_dos_read_call
description: Calls the DOS library read routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_write_call
description: Calls the DOS library write routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_input_call
description: Calls the DOS library input routine through the stored library base to obtain the standard input handle, and returns it.

name: forward_dos_output_call
description: Calls the DOS library output routine through the stored library base to obtain the standard output handle, and returns it.

name: prompt_yes_no_then_finish
description: Shows a prompt, reads a line of input and repeats until its first character is y, n, Y, N or a newline. When the answer is y or Y it calls a routine with the argument five, and it always finishes by calling a routine with zero.

name: count_string_length
description: Walks a zero-terminated string one byte at a time, counting bytes until the terminator, and returns the count.

description: Parses a command line for a background run: an optional -S switch with a number of at least 1600 is accepted, along with a digit flag, and then the named command is started in the background with its input and output sent to the null device. It returns a status code and reports invalid parameters.

name: start_main_program
description: Starts the main work from either a command-line invocation or a Workbench startup message. On the Workbench path it waits for and handles the startup message, while on the command-line path it splits the argument string into words, builds a pointer table, and calls the main routine with the word count and table, then returns zero.

name: finish_startup_with_status
description: Records its status argument and makes a call through the exec library vector. When an earlier step set a flag, it calls further exec routines to close a library and reply to the startup message, then returns the status.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers held at fixed negative offsets from a base register, then returns. No known caller reaches this entry, so it may be unused.

name: open_dos_library_with_setup
description: Opens the DOS library by name through the system library vector and returns the result if the open succeeded. On failure it runs a setup call, stores the value one hundred, runs cleanup calls when a flag is set, and returns that stored value.

name: forward_dos_write_call
description: Calls the DOS library write routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_input_call
description: Calls the DOS library input routine through the stored library base to obtain the standard input handle, and returns it.

name: forward_dos_output_call
description: Calls the DOS library output routine through the stored library base to obtain the standard output handle, and returns it.

name: forward_dos_ioerr_call
description: Calls the DOS library error-code routine through the stored library base and returns the error value it gives.

name: start_resident_tool_process
description: Starts a tool by finding its resident tag and creating a process for it, honouring a debug switch. It exchanges port messages with the workbench task and writes an error message when the tag cannot be found or the tool cannot start.

name: compare_strings_ordered
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings character by character. It returns zero when they match, minus one when the first string sorts lower, and one when it sorts higher.

name: allocate_linked_entry_chain
description: Walks a linked list, allocating a cleared memory block for each entry and duplicating a lock taken from the entry into it, then links the blocks together. It returns the first block, or zero if a step fails.

name: pass_params_to_subroutine
description: Calls another routine with a global variable, its own parameter, and the address of an eight-byte stack slot, then returns.

name: format_buffer_and_forward
description: Formats text with the operating system formatting routine into a local buffer, measures the resulting string, and when it is non-empty passes the buffer and its length on to another routine.

name: fill_handler_block_from_list

name: probe_clock_chip_then_dispatch
description: Checks for a clock chip at one of two fixed addresses, printing warnings when it is missing or found at the second address, and exits with a set code when no chip answers. It then reads the option arguments and either exits, prints usage, or runs a command through the execute routine.

name: print_setclock_usage
description: Prints three lines of usage text for the clock tool, covering its load and save options.

name: check_clock_chip_ticking
description: Reads a clock chip register, waits seventy-five ticks through a delay call, reads it again, and returns whether the low nibble changed.

name: query_timer_device_value
description: Sends a request with command number ten to the timer device through an I/O request block, waits for it to finish, returns the result stored in the request, and releases the block. It returns zero when no block is available.

name: set_timer_device_value
description: Sends a request with command number eleven to the timer device, passing a value from another routine, waits for completion, and releases the request. It returns minus one when no request block could be allocated.

name: open_timer_device_request
description: Creates a message port and an extended request block, then opens the timer device with the given unit number. On any failure it releases what it created and returns zero, otherwise it returns the request block.

name: close_timer_device_request
description: If given a request block, deletes its reply port when one exists, closes the device, and deletes the request block.

name: convert_clock_fields_to_seconds
description: Reads the clock-chip digit fields and combines them into a total count of seconds, adding days from a month table and yearly adjustments. It uses remainder and divide routines for the carries and returns the total.

name: split_seconds_into_clock_fields
description: Divides a total seconds count into calendar fields using divide and remainder routines, walks a month-length table to find the month, and stores each field in the clock buffer.

name: compare_strings_ignoring_case
description: Compares two zero-terminated strings after converting characters of the first to lower case. It returns zero when they match, minus one when the first sorts lower, and one otherwise.

name: compare_pending_char_order
description: Compares the character held in a data register with the byte at the address register. It returns zero when the register holds a zero byte, minus one when it sorts lower, and one otherwise.

name: classify_char_order_pair
description: Returns minus one when the character in the data register sorts below the byte at the address register, and one otherwise.

name: return_constant_one
description: Returns the value one and does nothing else.

name: convert_char_to_lower
description: Returns the character as a full-width value, with the upper-case letters A to Z converted to lower case by adding 32.

name: sign_extend_low_byte
description: Returns the low byte of the data register sign-extended to a full value.

name: write_fixed_pattern_sequence
description: Writes three fixed 32-bit patterns in sequence to a register at a fixed offset from a base pointer, then returns.

name: set_bits_and_poll_status
description: Sets a fixed mask of bits in a control word, then polls a status byte up to about two hundred times and returns as soon as the status bit it tests is clear.

name: clear_control_bits
description: Clears a fixed set of bits from a control word at a fixed offset from a base pointer, then returns.

name: print_formatted_message
description: Writes one formatted message to standard output through the C library formatted-print routine, passing its argument through, then returns.

name: forward_exec_allocmem_call
description: Calls the exec library memory allocation routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_exec_findtask_call
description: Calls the exec library find-task routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: divide_long_with_remainder
description: Divides a 32-bit value by a divisor and returns the quotient and remainder as a pair. Divisors above 16 bits use a 16-step shift-and-subtract loop, while smaller divisors use two 16-bit divisions.

name: multiply_32_bit_integers
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values by splitting them into 16-bit halves and summing the partial products. It returns the combined 32-bit product.

name: forward_unsigned_modulo_call
description: Calls the shared division routine and returns, leaving the remainder in the registers for the caller.

name: forward_unsigned_divide_call
description: Calls the shared division routine and returns the value it leaves in the second data register.

name: compute_signed_remainder
description: Calls the shared division routine and returns its remainder, negated when the sign flag held in an address register is non-zero.

name: compute_signed_quotient
description: Calls the shared division routine and returns its quotient, negated when the sign flag held in an address register is non-zero.

name: create_message_port
description: Allocates a signal bit and a 34-byte memory block, fills the port fields with the given name and the current task, and either adds the port to the public list or initializes an empty message list. It returns the block, or zero when a step fails.

name: delete_message_port
description: Removes the port from the public list when it is linked, marks it as deleted, frees its signal bit and releases its 34-byte memory block.

name: create_io_request
description: When given a reply port, allocates a memory block of the requested size, marks it as an I/O request, records the size and attaches the port. It returns the block, or zero when no port is given or allocation fails.

name: delete_io_request
description: Marks an I/O request as deleted, clears its link fields and frees its memory block using the size stored in the request. It does nothing for a zero pointer.

name: forward_formatted_output
description: Passes its format argument and the address of its variable arguments on to the formatted-output routine, then returns.

name: format_text_and_write
description: Formats text with the operating system formatting routine into a local 140-byte buffer, measures the result, and when it is non-empty writes it out through the write routine.

name: store_char_at_pointer
description: Stores the low byte of the data register at the address held in the address register, then returns. It serves as the character output callback for the formatting routine.

name: initialize_empty_list
description: Initializes an empty list header in the given block so its head points to the slot just after it, clears the count word, and points the tail back at the header.

name: run_timed_wait_command
description: Opens the DOS library and parses the command arguments for a period in seconds or minutes, or a time of day after the UNTIL keyword. It waits accordingly using timer and signal routines, prints a usage line when the arguments are missing or invalid, and returns a status.

name: call_and_accumulate_result
description: Calls one routine, then calls another for a value and adds that value to the integer stored at the address register, then returns.

name: split_sum_into_quotient
description: Adds a value to a stored accumulator, stores the remainder of that sum divided by a 16-bit divisor back into the accumulator, and returns the quotient, both truncated to 16 bits.

name: write_error_and_accumulate
description: Writes an error message through library output routines, then adds a value returned by another routine into the integer at the address register.

name: load_executable_hunks
description: Loads an AmigaDOS executable from its hunk list. It allocates memory for each hunk, copies code and data hunks into place, reserves zeroed space for BSS hunks, and applies 32-bit relocation entries by adding the load address.

name: return_without_action
description: Does nothing and returns. The body is a bare return with no calls or data access.

name: spin_delay_loop
description: Spins in a loop that decrements the data register until it wraps past zero, with no other work, then returns.

name: unpack_compressed_stream_backwards
description: Unpacks a compressed byte stream from run-length codes. Literal runs are copied from the input, and back-references copy earlier output bytes, with the output written from the end of the buffer toward its start.

name: decrement_byte_with_space_wrap
description: Decrements a byte held in a data register once per pass for a 16-bit count, replacing a zero result with a space character. It makes no memory accesses and returns without other effects.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The bytes at this entry are not valid code; the decompiler shows only a bad-instruction marker, so the routine has no behaviour of its own.

name: start_main_program
description: Starts the main work from either a command-line invocation or a Workbench startup message. On the Workbench path it waits for and handles the startup message, while on the command-line path it splits the argument string into words, builds a pointer table, and calls the main routine with the word count and table, then returns zero.

name: invoke_two_function_pointers
description: Calls two library routines through function pointers held at fixed negative offsets from a base register, then returns. No known caller reaches this entry, so it may be unused.

name: open_dos_library_with_setup
description: Opens the DOS library by name through the system library vector and returns the result if the open succeeded. On failure it runs a setup call, stores the value one hundred, runs cleanup calls when a flag is set, and returns that stored value.

name: forward_dos_open_call
description: Calls the DOS library open routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_close_call
description: Calls the DOS library close routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_input_call
description: Calls the DOS library input routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_output_call

name: forward_dos_lock_call

name: forward_dos_unlock_call
description: Calls the DOS library unlock routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_duplock_call
description: Calls the DOS library duplicate-lock routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_currentdir_call
description: Calls the DOS library current-directory routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_dos_execute_call
description: Calls the DOS library execute routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: open_console_window_for_cli
description: Opens a console window for a new command interpreter using the window specification and system path text. When started from the first branch it allocates and clears a 64-byte control block, and it frees that block again before returning.

name: allocate_bptr_entry_chain
description: Walks a linked list, allocating a cleared memory block for each entry, recording a value taken from the entry in the block, and linking the blocks together. It returns the first block as a BPTR value, the address divided by four.

name: free_bptr_entry_chain
description: Walks the chain built by the allocation routine, releasing each entry value through another routine and then freeing the 8-byte entry block.

name: forward_exec_allocmem_call
description: Calls the exec library memory allocation routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: forward_exec_findtask_call
description: Calls the exec library find-task routine through the stored library base and returns its result.

name: initialize_arp_library_base
description: Library code from arp.library that stores its argument in the library base, tries to open a dependent library up to a few times, and on success links a new structure into the base. On failure it calls a cleanup routine and returns.

name: collect_values_then_link_entry
description: Library code from arp.library that fills a buffer with values fetched through a library routine until one is zero or the counter runs out, then links a new structure into the base. It calls a cleanup routine on failure.

name: finish_library_entry_setup
description: Library code from arp.library that stores a pointer into the structure, makes three library calls to set up an entry, and on a non-zero result links it into the base. Otherwise it calls a cleanup routine.

name: poll_until_flag_then_count
description: Library code from arp.library that no known caller reaches. It repeats a library call until its condition flag clears, then increments a 16-bit counter in the structure.

name: clear_slot_then_call_library
description: Library code from arp.library. It zeroes a word-sized slot in the structure it is given and then makes one library call through the stored base.

name: allocate_block_with_link_word
description: Library code from arp.library that, when given a non-zero size, allocates a memory block and writes a link word into its first slot pointing just past that slot. A failed allocation leaves the block unchanged.

name: return_constant_zero

name: increment_counter_clear_bit
description: Library code from icon.library that increments a 16-bit counter in the structure and clears one flag bit in a byte of the same structure.

name: decrement_library_refcount
description: Library code from icon.library that decrements a 16-bit reference counter. When the count reaches zero and a flag bit is set it calls a cleanup routine and returns its result, otherwise it returns zero.

name: unlink_or_mark_pending
description: Library code from icon.library that, when a counter field is zero, calls a library routine, unlinks the structure from its list and returns the value it was given. Otherwise it sets a flag bit to mark the structure as pending and returns zero.

name: set_pending_flag_return_zero
description: Library code from icon.library that sets one flag bit in a byte of the structure and returns zero.

name: return_constant_zero

name: open_dos_library_into_globals
description: Library code from icon.library that stores its argument in the structure and opens the DOS library by name, copying two values into global variables on success and calling the alert routine on failure.

name: copy_two_values_into_globals
description: Library code from icon.library that copies two 32-bit values from fixed offsets in a structure, referenced by an address register, into two global variables.
